title: An IRQL rule checker
description:
Driver Verifier and static analysis tools catch IRQL mistakes. Write a simple checker for a sequence of operations a driver performs on one code path.

The code path starts at a given IRQL (0 PASSIVE, 1 APC, 2 DISPATCH, 3 and up device levels). Each operation is a string:

| Operation | Effect / rule |
|---|---|
| `"acquire_spinlock"` | Raises the IRQL to 2 (remember the old level). Not allowed above 2 |
| `"release_spinlock"` | Restores the IRQL from before the matching acquire. Not allowed without a matching acquire |
| `"wait"` | Only allowed below 2 |
| `"touch_paged"` | Only allowed below 2 |
| `"touch_nonpaged"` | Always allowed |
| `"call_pageable"` | Only allowed below 2 |

Write `checkPath(startIrql, ops)`, returning a list of problems, each `"step N: OPERATION at IRQL L"` (N from 1). When an operation is not allowed, report it and carry on as if it had happened (a release without an acquire leaves the IRQL unchanged). At the end, if spin locks are still held, add `"end: N spin lock(s) still held"`.
hints: Keep the current IRQL and a stack of saved IRQLs, one per spin lock held. Check each operation against the current IRQL before applying its effect.
Acquiring pushes the current IRQL and sets 2; releasing pops and restores, if there is anything to pop.
